title: Agent spawn refusal must not leak the session credential
description:
Objective: make the Windows spawn-argument refusal fail closed WITHOUT leaving the agent's session credential on disk.

RAISED BY: governor-18a42000 audit of commit 71fd5a0, 2026-08-15, at the human's direction. That commit landed with NO task id and therefore NO QA review against a DoD. It is otherwise good work — it correctly replaces a deprecated argv-plus-shell spawn (DEP0190) with a built command line and a fail-closed guard. The defect is in what the new refusal path skips.

MEASURED DEFECT, re-measure before planning. In apps/daemon/src/orchestrator/agent-wrapper-main.ts, function claudeSpawner:

1. `writeFileSync(mcpConfigPath, JSON.stringify({ mcpServers: { "moe-next": { env: { ...storeEnv, MOE_SESSION_CREDENTIAL: request.credential } } } }), "utf8")` writes the agent's credential to disk FIRST.
2. `return new Promise((resolve) => { const invocation = agentSpawnInvocation(command, [...]); ... })`.
3. `agentSpawnInvocation` -> `quoteForCmd` THROWS `SPAWN_ARGUMENT_UNQUOTABLE` when an argument matches `/["%&|<>^\r\n]/u` (apps/daemon/src/orchestrator/agent-spawn-invocation.ts).
4. The throw occurs inside the Promise executor, so the promise REJECTS. `const finish = () => { rmSync(mcpConfigPath, { force: true }); resolve(); }` is declared after the spawn and is only wired to child exit/error, so it is never installed and NEVER RUNS.
5. The credential file remains on disk.

The file's own comment states the invariant this breaks: "The config file carries the agent's credential; it must not outlive the agent it was minted for. Both exit paths remove it." There is a THIRD exit path and it removes nothing.

REACHABILITY, and why this is not theoretical. `mcpConfigPath = join(mkdtempSync(join(tmpdir(), "moe-wrapper-")), request.sessionId + ".json")`. On Windows `tmpdir()` resolves under the user profile. A Windows profile folder containing `&`, `^`, `%`, `<`, `>`, `|` or `"` — for example `C:\Users\Bob & Alice\AppData\Local\Temp` — makes EVERY agent spawn throw, leaking one credential file per spawn attempt. No hostile input is required, only an ordinary account name.

SEVERITY IS BOUNDED BUT REAL. Line 42 registers `process.once("exit", () => rmSync(configDir, { force: true, recursive: true }))`, so files clear when the wrapper process ends. But the wrapper is long-lived and polls on MOE_WRAPPER_INTERVAL_MS (default 15000), so credentials persist for the wrapper's remaining lifetime rather than an agent's seconds, and `process.once("exit")` does not run on SIGKILL or a hard crash.

RECOMMENDED SHAPE, not binding: validate the arguments BEFORE minting the credential to disk — hoist the `agentSpawnInvocation(...)` call above the `writeFileSync`. That is cheaper and stricter than a try/finally, because it means no credential is ever written for a request that cannot be spawned. If try/finally is chosen instead, the cleanup must cover the throw path explicitly and the test must prove it.

SECOND, SMALLER DEFECT IN THE SAME COMMIT: the refusal is `throw new Error(\`SPAWN_ARGUMENT_UNQUOTABLE: ${argument}\`)` — an unstructured message, not a stable reason code with a named refusing layer. Its test asserts `/SPAWN_ARGUMENT_UNQUOTABLE/u`, a REGEX ON A MESSAGE STRING. Under the assert-the-reason-code rail a refusal test must pin the exact stable code and the layer that refused; a message regex silently passes if the message is reworded and proves nothing about which layer answered. The message also interpolates the full argument, which is the config path here — not secret today, but it is a refusal echoing its input.

NOT IN SCOPE: changing the DEP0190 fix itself, the quoting strategy, the UNQUOTABLE character set, non-Windows spawn behaviour, or the wrapper's polling loop. If the character set looks wrong to you, raise it separately rather than widening this task.

Verification: pnpm --filter @moe/daemon typecheck && pnpm --filter @moe/daemon test.
definitionOfDone: No credential file exists on disk after a refused spawn: a test drives claudeSpawner with an argument that trips the guard, and asserts the mcpConfigPath does NOT exist afterwards. The assertion is on the filesystem, not on a mock of it.
The refusal carries an exact stable reason code AND names the refusing layer, asserted by a test that pins both values literally rather than matching a regex against an Error message.

The existing behaviour is unchanged on every non-refusing path: non-Windows spawns still return {args, file, shell:false} with argv intact; Windows spawns still collapse to one command line; the whitespace-quoting case still quotes; and the existing agent-spawn-invocation.test.ts cases stay green as written.
The credential is never written for a request that cannot be spawned - proven by asserting the write did not happen at all on the refusal path, not merely that a later delete occurred.

A mutation drill proves the new coverage is load-bearing: reverting the fix (restoring the original ordering) turns a NAMED test red on the credential-presence assertion, and the drill is restored byte-exact afterwards.
Fresh pnpm --filter @moe/daemon typecheck && pnpm --filter @moe/daemon test exits 0, with each leg's exit code read separately.
taskRails: This is a credential-handling path. The fix must ensure no credential is written for a request that cannot be spawned - do not settle for deleting it afterwards, which leaves a window.
Every refusal test pins the exact stable reason code and the layer that refused. A regex against an Error message does not satisfy this rail and is the specific weakness being corrected here.
Do not change the DEP0190 fix, the quoting strategy, or the UNQUOTABLE character set. If you believe the character set is wrong, raise a separate task rather than widening this one.

Re-measure agent-wrapper-main.ts and agent-spawn-invocation.ts on current bytes before editing; commit 71fd5a0 is recent and the shared worktree moves. Preserve foreign work and commit only explicit owned paths.
Do not let a refusal echo its input. The current message interpolates the full argument; the replacement should carry the stable code and layer without reproducing the path.

implementationPlan.description:
TDD — WRITE THE FAILING CREDENTIAL-LEAK TEST FIRST, extending the existing `apps/daemon/src/orchestrator/agent-spawner.test.ts` (do not add a new file).

Drive `claudeSpawner` with an argument that trips the guard and assert the credential file is NOT on disk afterwards. Requirements that decide whether this test is worth anything:

- ASSERT AGAINST THE REAL FILESYSTEM (DoD 1). AgentSpawnerOptions exposes only `command`, `log` and `spawn` — there is no fs injection, so use `existsSync`/`readdirSync` on the actual config directory. A mock of fs would not satisfy the DoD.
- CAPTURE THE ACTUAL CONFIG DIR. It comes from `mkdtempSync` at spawner-construction time, so construct the spawner INSIDE the test and determine the exact path it used. A test that guesses or hardcodes a temp path passes for the wrong reason.
- FORCE THE WIN32 PATH. `agentSpawnInvocation` returns early for every non-win32 platform (:33), so on a Linux or macOS runner a refusal test that does not force the platform NEVER REACHES THE GUARD and passes while testing nothing. Make the win32 path explicit.
- ASSERT THE REFUSAL ARRIVES AS A REJECTION, not a synchronous throw: `await expect(...).rejects...`. A bare try/catch would pass under either channel and would hide the regression step 4 must avoid.
- Assert the config directory contains NO leftover file at all, not merely that one named path is gone.

This test must FAIL now, on the current ordering. If it passes before step 4, it is not reaching the guard — fix the test before continuing.

implementationPlan.note:
PRODUCTION (agent-spawn-invocation.ts, 36 -> 58 lines). Replaced the bare `throw new Error(`SPAWN_ARGUMENT_UNQUOTABLE: ${argument}`)` with, following the daemon's existing convention in packages/scheduler/src/graph-analysis-error.ts (public readonly code + this.name):

  export type SpawnInvocationRefusalCode = "SPAWN_ARGUMENT_UNQUOTABLE";   // closed union
  export const SPAWN_INVOCATION_LAYER = "agent-spawn-invocation";
  export class SpawnInvocationRefusal extends Error {
    public readonly code: SpawnInvocationRefusalCode;
    public readonly layer: string;
    constructor(code) { super(code); this.name = "SpawnInvocationRefusal"; this.code = code; this.layer = SPAWN_INVOCATION_LAYER; }
  }
  ... throw new SpawnInvocationRefusal("SPAWN_ARGUMENT_UNQUOTABLE");

implementationPlan.description:
THE FIX — HOIST THE GUARD ABOVE THE CREDENTIAL WRITE, in `apps/daemon/src/orchestrator/agent-spawner.ts`.

Move the `agentSpawnInvocation(command, [...])` call from :63-67 to ABOVE the `writeFileSync` at :45. `mcpConfigPath` is computed at :42 and does not depend on the write, so the invocation can be built first. Result: a request that cannot be spawned never causes a credential to reach disk at all — strictly stronger than deleting it afterwards, which is what task rail 1 requires.

PRESERVE THE REJECTION CONTRACT — this is the regression a naive hoist ships. Today the throw is inside `return new Promise((resolve) => {...})`, so it surfaces as a promise REJECTION. Hoisted above the `return`, the same throw escapes SYNCHRONOUSLY from a function typed `(request: SpawnRequest) => Promise<void>`, and any caller using `.catch()` without `await` silently stops catching it. Make the returned arrow `async` so throws become rejections, or wrap the hoisted call equivalently. Use what step 1 recorded about the real call site to confirm, and let the step-2 rejection assertion prove it.

Keep the existing cleanup exactly as it is: `finish` at :77-80 and its two installations at :81 and :85 still handle the spawned-child paths. This step removes the THIRD exit path by making it unreachable, not by adding a fourth cleanup.

Do not touch the `process.once("exit")` sweep at :37, the DEP0190 handling, or the polling loop.

Run the step-2 test; it must now pass. Run the full agent-spawner.test.ts and agent-spawn-invocation.test.ts; every pre-existing case must still pass, including the two regex assertions.

The refusal now strictly PRECEDES the write, so a request that cannot be spawned never causes a credential to reach disk at all. This removes the third exit path by making it unreachable rather than adding a fourth cleanup — `finish` and its three installations (timeout, exit, error) are byte-unchanged.

THREE THINGS THE HOIST REQUIRED, each deliberate:

1. `async` on the returned arrow. This is the regression a naive hoist ships and step 1 measured the call site to settle it: agent-wrapper.ts:226 does `config.spawnAgent({...}).catch(() => undefined).then(...)` with NO await. Hoisted out of the Promise executor, the same throw would escape synchronously out of staff() and out of runOnce()'s for-loop and crash the poll tick, and .catch() would never see it. `async` converts it back to a rejection. The step-2 case pins this with `expect(() => { returned = spawner(req); }).not.toThrow()` followed by `await expect(returned).rejects...`, so the contract is asserted, not assumed. The comment at :53-56 records why the keyword is load-bearing so it is not "cleaned up" later.

2. `new Promise<void>` explicit type parameter — inside an async function the contextual return type no longer pins it, and the bare form would infer `Promise<unknown>`.

3. `platform` is now passed as agentSpawnInvocation's third argument. That option ALREADY existed (AgentSpawnerOptions.platform, resolved at :52 as `options.platform ?? process.platform`) and was read only by killTree; agentSpawnInvocation was falling back to its own `process.platform` default. Production behaviour is identical (same value, same source). It is what lets the refusal test force win32 without mutating a global — without it that case reaches no guard at all on a Linux/macOS runner and passes while testing nothing, the exact vacuous shape the epic's reason-code rail names. Not one of the four rail-3 forbidden surfaces: the DEP0190 line construction, the quoting strategy, the UNQUOTABLE set and the non-win32 early return are all untouched, as are process.once("exit") at :45 and the polling loop.

comments.content:
⚠️ SECOND DEFECT ON THIS EXACT REFUSAL PATH — READ BEFORE EXECUTING THE PLAN. From governor-18a42000's adversarial audit of today's diff (7 lenses, 35 findings raised, 36 skeptic verdicts). This one survived BOTH skeptics with ZERO kills — the strongest result in the whole sweep.

THE DEFECT: when `agentSpawnInvocation` throws SPAWN_ARGUMENT_UNQUOTABLE, the wrapper reports the agent as SPAWNED even though no process was ever created.

apps/daemon/src/orchestrator/agent-wrapper.ts:226-231, verified on current bytes:

    const exit = config.spawnAgent({ ... })
      .catch(() => undefined).then(() => { active.delete(workItemId); });
    active.set(workItemId, exit);
    return { kind: step.kind, outcome: "SPAWNED", sessionId, workItemId };

The throw happens inside the Promise executor, so the promise REJECTS. `.catch(() => undefined)` swallows it whole — no code, no log, no record — and the function returns `outcome: "SPAWNED"` unconditionally. The board is then told an agent is running that does not exist. That is a fail-open on the orchestration path, and it is arguably worse than the credential leak this task was filed for: a leaked file is recoverable, a phantom SPAWNED is a lie the scheduler acts on.

**THE INTERACTION THAT MATTERS TO YOUR PLAN — this is why I am posting rather than filing separately.** This task's recommended fix is to hoist `agentSpawnInvocation(...)` ABOVE the `writeFileSync` so no credential is minted for an unspawnable request. That is still the right fix. But note what it does to the throw:

- Hoisted ABOVE `return new Promise(...)` -> the throw becomes SYNCHRONOUS from `config.spawnAgent(...)`. The `.catch()` at :229 is chained to the RETURN VALUE and is never attached, so the throw propagates out of `dispatch` and can take down the wrapper loop instead of being swallowed.
- Hoisted but still INSIDE the executor -> unchanged: still swallowed, still reports SPAWNED.

Either way the refusal does not reach anyone who can act on it. **Fixing the credential leak without addressing this converts a silent lie into a crash, or leaves the lie in place.** Please handle both, or explicitly report which you are deferring and why, so the second half is not silently dropped — that exact half-fix pattern is what produced task-70b6361d earlier today.

WHAT A CORRECT ANSWER LOOKS LIKE: a refused spawn must be reported as a refusal with its exact stable reason code and layer, distinguishable from SPAWNED by the caller. A blanket `.catch(() => undefined)` on a path that can carry an authority refusal is the anti-pattern — it is indistinguishable from success and it is the reason no test caught this.

SECOND, LOWER-CONFIDENCE FINDING on your other owned file, one skeptic of two (so weigh it yourself rather than taking it as given): `quoteForCmd` at agent-spawn-invocation.ts:25 may fail OPEN on an argument that contains whitespace AND ends with a backslash. `UNQUOTABLE` is `/["%&|<>^\r\n]/u` and the quote step is `/\s/u.test(argument) ? \`"${argument}"\` : argument`. A trailing backslash yields `"...\"` — cmd.exe does not treat `\` as an escape, so its quote tracking is satisfied and the argument mis-parses rather than being refused. Parentheses are also absent from UNQUOTABLE. Your task rail forbids changing the UNQUOTABLE set, so if you judge this real, RAISE IT SEPARATELY rather than widening this task.

I have not edited any file. Four agents are working in this shared worktree.

planningNotes.approachesConsidered:
HOIST, NOT try/finally — and the task's own recommendation is correct for a reason worth stating. A try/finally around the write would delete the credential after a refusal, but it would still WRITE it first, leaving a window in which the file exists on disk for a request that was never spawnable. Hoisting `agentSpawnInvocation(...)` above `writeFileSync` means no credential is ever minted for a request that cannot run — strictly stronger, and cheaper. Task rail 1 requires exactly this: "do not settle for deleting it afterwards, which leaves a window."

THE HOIST INTRODUCES A TRAP THAT A NAIVE FIX WILL SHIP. Today the throw happens INSIDE `return new Promise((resolve) => {...})` at agent-spawner.ts:57-67, so it surfaces as a promise REJECTION. Move the call above the `return` and the same throw escapes SYNCHRONOUSLY from a function whose declared type is `(request: SpawnRequest) => Promise<void>`. A caller that writes `spawnAgent(req).catch(...)` without `await` would stop catching it, and the failure would become an unhandled synchronous throw in the wrapper's poll loop. The fix must preserve the rejection contract — make the returned arrow `async` (any throw inside then becomes a rejection) or wrap the hoisted call so it rejects — and a test must pin that the refusal still arrives as a REJECTION, not a sync throw. Verify the real call site (agent-wrapper-main.ts:85 passes it as `spawnAgent`) before choosing.

STRUCTURED REFUSAL THAT KEEPS THE EXISTING TESTS GREEN. agent-spawn-invocation.test.ts:41 and :44 assert `toThrow(/SPAWN_ARGUMENT_UNQUOTABLE/u)`, a regex against the Error MESSAGE, and DoD 3 requires those cases to stay green AS WRITTEN. So the replacement must carry `code` and `layer` as real properties while leaving the literal token `SPAWN_ARGUMENT_UNQUOTABLE` in the message. Dropping the `: ${argument}` suffix (task rail 5, no refusal echoing its input) does not disturb the regex, which only looks for the token. This is the one shape that satisfies DoD 2 and DoD 3 simultaneously; a message rewritten to something else would redden two existing tests and a message keeping the argument would violate rail 5.

REJECTED: adding a new test file. Both `agent-spawner.test.ts` and `agent-spawn-invocation.test.ts` already exist, so the work extends them. Also rejected: touching the UNQUOTABLE character set, the quoting strategy or the DEP0190 fix — task rail 3 forbids it and the description says to raise a separate task if the set looks wrong.

planningNotes.risks:
DoD 4 CANNOT BE PROVEN BY AN ABSENCE ASSERTION ALONE, and this is the subtlest part of the task. "No file exists afterwards" is satisfied EQUALLY by 'never written' and by 'written then deleted' — the two outcomes DoD 4 exists to distinguish, since only the first closes the window. A test that just checks absence would pass against a try/finally fix that still writes the credential first.

THE INSTRUMENT IS A NEGATIVE-CONTROL DRILL: temporarily disable the cleanup entirely (remove the `rmSync` from `finish`, or the `process.once("exit")` sweep), re-run the refusal test, and confirm the file STILL never appears. If it appears once cleanup is disabled, the credential was being written and deleted, not never written — and the fix is the wrong shape. Record this drill's output; it is the only evidence that separates the two.

THE SYNC-THROW REGRESSION is the second trap. Hoisting moves the throw out of the Promise executor, converting a rejection into a synchronous throw from a `Promise<void>`-typed function. Pin the rejection contract with a test that awaits a rejection (`await expect(spawn(req)).rejects...`), not a try/catch that would pass either way.

THE REAL FILESYSTEM MAKES THE TEST ORDER-SENSITIVE. `configDir` comes from `mkdtempSync` at spawner-construction time, and `process.once("exit")` registers a sweep per construction. Construct the spawner inside the test (not in a describe body), capture the config dir it used, and assert against that exact path — a test that guesses the temp path or shares one across cases will pass for the wrong reason.
